text: The executive summary reports that continuous fitness predicts essentiality better than essentiality_fraction (AUC=0.70-0.73 versus AUC<0.5).

heading: Executive Summary

text: The 478-gene triple-covered sample excludes TnSeq-essential genes, limiting its FBA–growth comparison to TnSeq-dispensable genes.
quote: All 478 triple-covered genes (having TnSeq + FBA + growth data) are **TnSeq-dispensable** on minimal media. This is biologically expected — TnSeq-essential genes have no viable deletion mutants, so they cannot have growth rate measurements. The analysis therefore asks: **among dispensable genes, does FBA correctly predict which ones matter for growth?**

heading: Finding 1: FBA Does Not Predict Growth Defects Among TnSeq-Dispensable Genes

text: Among 478 TnSeq-dispensable genes, FBA class was not associated with growth defects (chi-squared = 0.93, p = 0.63, 2 df); class-specific rates were 73.1% (57/78), 73.5% (150/204), and 69.4% (136/196).
quote:
Among 478 triple-covered genes (all TnSeq-dispensable), FBA class was **not significantly associated** with growth defect status (chi-squared = 0.93, p = 0.63, 2 df). Growth defect rates were nearly identical across FBA classes:
- **FBA-essential**: 73.1% (57/78 genes)
- **FBA-variable**: 73.5% (150/204 genes)
- **FBA-blocked**: 69.4% (136/196 genes)
heading: Finding 1: FBA Does Not Predict Growth Defects Among TnSeq-Dispensable Genes

text: Mean growth rates did not significantly differ by FBA class (Kruskal-Wallis H = 1.67, p = 0.43).
quote: The Kruskal-Wallis test on mean growth rates was also non-significant (H = 1.67, p = 0.43).
heading: Finding 1: FBA Does Not Predict Growth Defects Among TnSeq-Dispensable Genes

heading: Finding 2: The Null Result Is Robust Across Growth Defect Thresholds

text: The FBA-class null persisted through Q35; Q40 produced a marginal p = 0.048 association, while the continuous-rate test remained nonsignificant.
quote: The chi-squared p-value remained above 0.05 for thresholds Q10–Q35. Only at Q40 did a marginal association appear (p = 0.048), driven by a slight divergence in FBA-essential vs FBA-blocked defect rates (90% vs 81%). The threshold-independent Kruskal-Wallis test on continuous mean growth rates confirms no association (H = 1.67, p = 0.43).

text: In the original ADP1 analysis of 478 triple-covered, TnSeq-dispensable genes in minimal media, FBA class showed no detected association with growth-defect status across the tested carbon-source conditions (p=0.63); the null result does not apply to dispensable genes generally.

text: The report interprets TnSeq as measuring fitness cost rather than lethality; at the 0.05 TnSeq threshold versus rich-media knockout calls among 1,933 genes, 211 knockout-essential genes were TnSeq-dispensable.

text: Partial function from transposon-disrupted alleles is a proposed explanation for TnSeq–knockout discordance, not a demonstrated cause.

text: Aggregated TnSeq essentiality fraction mixes experimental conditions; condition-matched comparisons may be more informative.

Essentiality fraction mixes diverse conditions

text: Regressing continuous FBA flux against growth rate is proposed to test effects that binary essentiality classes may miss.

   - Separate condition effects from method effects
